Manoj S Nair : Onboarding Steps for Jems
• Subscribe to @JemsBot and give first jems from Cliq Web version for hassle free onboarding.
• Whenever prompted grant permission to access your Zoho profile for various Zoho services.
• You can use "Give" menu in the bot to start giving Jems. You can also pin JemsBot for better access in future. /jems command can also be used in any conversation to open Give Jems form in Zoho Cliq (Secondary method).
• You won't be able to give Jems to users who are not part of your Jems portal.
• When Jems privacy is set as "secret" Jems message will be posted in the Direct Message with the recipient. Default option "private" will post an additional message publicly to your team's/portal's Cliq channel. The option "public" will mark the Jems transaction to be featured in an org-wide feed (Future Update).
• If you are part of multiple Jems portals, you can change your default portal in "Settings" sub-menu listed in "Help" menu next to "Give" Jems menu.
• To know more about Jems, Categories you can use "What is Jems?" in "Help" menu.
• If you want to contact Jems Support, you can make use of "App Feedback" in "Help" menu.

Multiple High and Critical severity vulnerabilities have been identified globally in widely used web browsers, including Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, and Microsoft Edge , posing a significant security risk if left unpatched. These vulnerabilities span across 2025 and 2026 releases. Based on our assessment, the vulnerabilities include (but are not limited to): Memory Corruption Buffer Overflow Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) Privilege Escalation Denial of Service Information Disclosure Code Execution & Security Bypass issues These issues pose a high risk of exploitation, including remote code execution and data leakage, if not patched in a timely manner. Nithya Kumar has commented on a post in Zoho Corp Wall.
Objective Form Enhancement – External Audit NC Closure (ISO 9001:2015)
Since the Planned Percentage field has been newly added to the Objective form, the Completion Percentage must follow specific rules. If the objective is completed before the ETA , the Completion Percentage cannot exceed the Planned Percentage and must exactly match it in order to close the objective. If the objective is not completed before the ETA or if the ETA has been exceeded , the Completion Percentage must be entered below the Planned Percentage . Only then will a child objective be created . If the Completion Percentage is entered equal to the Planned Percentage in this case, the child objective will not be created and the remaining work will not be tracked. Example: If the Planned Percentage is 70% and only 50% of that planned work is completed, the Completion Percentage should be entered as 35% (not 50%). Sherrin J V has commented on a post in the Group, Arattai Feedback.
After E2EE is enabled, the conversation splits into two threads. Old (non-E2EE) messages are not visible in the new encrypted chat, even though new replies are part of the same conversation. This disrupts conversation continuity and leads to a loss o...
Thanks for sharing this feedback. The separation between non-E2EE and E2EE messages is intentional and by design. When E2EE is enabled, we create a clear boundary between messages that were sent without encryption and those that are fully end-to-end encrypted. This avoids any confusion about which messages are protected under E2EE and maintains strong security guarantees. Going forward, all active and future conversations are prioritized in the E2EE chat . The older non-E2EE thread is sidelined and kept only for reference , so users can still access past messages when needed, but new communication continues securely in the encrypted thread. This approach ensures clarity, security, and a consistent experience as conversations move to E2EE by default.
